goal: Make project-owned verification process discovery work on Linux hosts so deterministic QA can prove cleanup there, without weakening the macOS/BSD scanner path or the fail-closed cleanup guarantee.

acceptance.assertion: Token discovery is platform-native: Linux discovery reads each candidate process environment from procfs instead of invoking ps, so the real-execution verification suites pass on the existing tests, while a synthetic procfs fixture proves the Linux branch selects exactly the token-carrying processes and an unreadable proc root still yields a cleanup failure instead of a passed check.

Deterministic QA aggregation and the Pi/Claude real-port conformance group named project-owned-verification execute unknown project commands with explicit bounded preparation and pass on the fixed discovery path.
The canary assurance authority seam runs fixed verification descriptors end to end and still produces only host-attested QA evidence.
The generated Claude host bundle is byte-in-sync with the runtime source that carries the platform-native discovery branch.
Workspace type checking passes with the platform branch and the injected proc-root discovery seam.
